text:
Alex: heads up — saw a streaming response abruptly cut when a preemptible GPU was evicted. client reported ~300 tokens missing, no resume.
Priya: ugh. which pool/region?
Alex: eu-west1, pool ephemeral-gpu-spot-2, instance g4dnx-2 (preemptible). thread_ts=1782345678
Marco: we had a pattern like this last week when kubelet kills before preStop finishes. the cloud notifies 30s but our pod grace was 10s.
Jen: was there any checkpointing of the token stream? i.e. last-acked token persisted somewhere?
Alex: no — streaming is in-memory pipeline + KV cache local to pod. if pod dies we lose last ephemeral tokens.
Priya: that explains it. options: (A) extend terminationGrace + preStop drain hook, (B) checkpoint streaming progress to a central store during open stream, (C) route long-lived streams to non-preemptible pool.
Marco: config we use now (short):
```
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["/bin/true"]
```
we should change to:
```
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120
lifecycle:
  preStop:
    exec:
      command: ["sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/drain-hook.sh"]
```
Jen: drain-hook.sh should send a QUIT to runtime, flush KV caches, and write last-offset to redis before exiting.
Alex: agree. but edge cases: if the node is reclaimed instantly (rare) the container won't get full grace. cloud preemptible docs say notification window is best-effort.
Marco: true — can't rely on it 100%. need fallback. suggestion: introduce request-level requeue with idempotency keys + client resume token.
Priya: i like client resume token + server-side durable checkpoint. overall flow:
- client opens stream with resume_id
- server periodically persists last_sent_token_index for resume_id
- on pod eviction, other pod takes over and resumes from persisted index

Jen: that requires fast metadata path. redis/placement should be regional and low-latency. add TTL + last-write-wins.
Alex: concern: duplicated tokens if we requeue without dedupe on client. need idempotency model.
Marco: implement server-assigned sequence numbers per stream and client ignore duplicates using seq > last_ack.
Priya: another angle: mixed-capacity pools. route streams longer than X seconds to dedicated capacity, keep short requests on preemptible. saves cost while protecting long sessions.
Jen: yes — routing policy: if predicted_tokens > 500 or expected_duration > 15s => route to dedicated. predictive model can be cheap NLP on prompt length.
Alex: cost tradeoffs: dedicated is 3-4x on VM cost but reduces resume complexity for long streams.
Priya: telemetry needed: histogram of stream durations, eviction rate by pool, time-to-resume failures. I can add metrics to /model/streaming.*
Marco: also add kube event alert: if preemptible evictions spike > 5/min in a region -> autoscaler should slow drains and increase dedicated headroom.
DeployBot: autoscaler: scaled down ephemeral-gpu-spot-2 from 40 -> 32 at 2026-02-24T03:14:12Z due to underutilization :gear: 
SRE-Bot: alert: preemptible-eviction-rate eu-west1 = 8/min over 5m window
Alex: next: PoC plan I propose:
1) make preStop write last_offset to redis and set terminationGrace 120s (Marco)
2) implement resume API + client idempotency (Jen)
3) routing rule prototype for long streams -> dedicated (Priya)
4) metrics + alerting (Alex)

Marco: i'll prepare PR for kube manifest change and drain-hook. will test with local kill flow.
Jen: i'll spec the resume API and client-side sample. simple endpoints: POST /streams/:id/resume -> {from_index}
Priya: i'll add the routing flag and add telemetry + SLO for resume-success-rate.
Alex: timeline? can we get a small end-to-end PoC within 2 weeks?
Priya: yes — routing + metrics in 1 week, resume API + client sample in 2.
Marco: i'll roll kube change behind feature flag and add chaos test that sends SIGTERM at random times.
Jen: note on implementation detail: persist every N tokens (e.g., every 16 tokens) to avoid too much write amplification.
Alex: ok. after PoC we'll evaluate cost delta for routing and decide steady-state mix: expected ~25% long streams -> dedicated commit maybe.
Priya: added task cards in #eng-runtime-board. @Alex assign ownership?
Alex: assigned to me for tracking. thanks everyone :thumbsup: 
Jen: quick debug snippet for dedupe logic:
```
if incoming.seq <= persisted.last_ack_seq:
  ignore
else:
  emit and persist
```
Marco: also capture node metadata on persist (node_id, pod_id) for forensic.
SRE-Bot: noted. created incident tracker INCT-2026-042 for stream-resume feature work.
Alex: good thread. will follow up with PoC PRs and testing notes. closing for now.
